purpose: Sign-specific two-part Calendar cards composed from the owner-approved meaning components. Each card carries a forecast the reader can use and a Details explanation underneath.
servingRule: Both ownerApproved and servingAuthorized must be true. Anything else is invisible to the runtime and the Calendar falls through to the existing exact body for that planet pair and aspect.
storedBodyConvention: forecast begins lowercase; the Calendar composes the date lead-in. details begins with the transit label, for example 'Sun in Leo opposite Saturn in Aquarius.'

cards.forecast: a cause people believe in finds an opening with the group that has been asking who the current setup actually serves. Belief travels faster than proof here, so an argument can gather support before anyone has shown the numbers behind it. Nobody is required to take the opening, and it closes quietly if no one does. One concrete step, taken where people can see it, is what turns sympathy into a change in the rules.
cards.details: Neptune in Aries sextile Pluto in Aquarius. A cause people believe in meets a group already asking who the current arrangement serves. Neptune in Aries supplies an ideal worth starting now, and Pluto in Aquarius supplies the pressure that exposes who holds power inside a system. Because this is a sextile the opening is offered rather than automatic, and an urgent push meeting a structure built to hold means the workable move is the one that fits what the system will not give up.

cards.forecast: one piece of information changes what looks possible, and a plan people already wanted starts to look reachable. Enthusiasm arrives ahead of the details, so the version being repeated may be further along than the version anyone can check. Nobody has to act on it, and the opening closes quietly if no one does. What moves it is a decision with a date attached for checking whether the new information held.
cards.details: Uranus in Gemini sextile Neptune in Aries. New information lands and a hoped-for plan suddenly looks reachable. Uranus in Gemini keeps rewriting the available routes as the facts change, while Neptune in Aries supplies the belief that makes starting feel clearer than the evidence warrants. A sextile offers the connection without forcing it, and since the facts are still moving while the appetite to begin is not, a decision holds only if it names the day it gets checked again.

cards.forecast: a different explanation lines up with a long push to change who the rules favor, so an argument that used to stall starts travelling. Agreement comes easily enough that a weak assumption can ride along unexamined. The wording keeps getting revised while the requirement underneath it stays unnamed. Progress depends on somebody stating that requirement plainly, so the revisions have something to answer to.
cards.details: Uranus in Gemini trine Pluto in Aquarius. A newer explanation lines up with a longer push to change who the rules favor. Uranus in Gemini changes the terms as information lands; Pluto in Aquarius concentrates on the power a system keeps distributing. Trines meet little resistance, and because the language can be rewritten while the underlying requirement cannot, the requirement has to be said out loud before the rewrites amount to anything.

cards.forecast: public backing and a hard deadline turn up in the same week, which makes an ambitious plan look more credible than it did a month ago. Support and limits agree for once, so what gets promised has a decent chance of being delivered. The ease is the risk: applause makes it tempting to promise a size the schedule cannot carry. What holds is a commitment scoped to what the deadline allows.
cards.details: Jupiter in Leo trine Saturn in Aries. Visible support and a firm deadline arrive together. Jupiter in Leo enlarges what generous backing can do for somebody's contribution, and Saturn in Aries supplies the deadline that decides how much of it can actually be built. The trine lets both work toward the same result, though fire on both sides can make speed feel like proof, so the scope has to fit the schedule rather than the enthusiasm.

cards.forecast: a deadline nobody enjoys turns out to be the thing that finally gets an old arrangement examined. Once a date is attached, people start asking who the current setup was built to protect, and that question is easier to answer with a schedule than without one. The opening is available rather than automatic, and it closes again if everyone waits for somebody else to raise it. Naming the one limit the new arrangement has to respect is what turns the question into a change.
cards.details: Saturn in Aries sextile Pluto in Aquarius. A firm deadline gives a group the occasion to ask who the current arrangement actually serves. Saturn in Aries sets how fast a first move is allowed to go, while Pluto in Aquarius works on who holds power inside a system many people share. A sextile offers that combination rather than forcing it, and since a date forces movement while the arrangement is built not to give, the pressure gathers on the arrangement rather than on who argues hardest.

cards.forecast: somebody steps forward on a piece of work and is handed a bigger part of it in the same week. Effort and standing stop being separate questions: the more visible the push, the larger the role that follows, and the larger the role, the harder it becomes to slow down. Nobody involved is likely to want the smaller version. The distinction worth keeping is between what one person can personally carry and what the group has started expecting them to.
cards.details: Mars in Leo conjunct Jupiter in Leo. One person's push and one person's growing role arrive as a single event. Mars in Leo puts effort where it will be seen and named, and Jupiter in Leo enlarges what that visibility can be turned into. A conjunction fuses the two, so any move on one is a move on the other, and with both in a fixed fire sign the appetite grows faster than anyone stops to check it.

cards.forecast: a plan with a hard date meets information that keeps changing underneath it. Each update makes the old route look wrong and the deadline look less negotiable, so people are choosing between committing to something that may be revised and waiting for facts that may not hold still in time. Neither choice is being forced. The commitment holds only if it says in advance what would justify changing it.
cards.details: Saturn in Aries sextile Uranus in Gemini. A deadline and a stream of revised information land on the same plan. Saturn in Aries sets what a rushed start has to prove before it counts, while Uranus in Gemini keeps rewriting the options as new facts arrive. The sextile connects them without forcing the issue, and since a decision is being pressed while conditions underneath it will not hold still, what survives is a decision that carries its own review point.

What passes unexamined is whether the size of the promise was ever measured against the time available. Work scoped to the date gets finished, and work scoped to the enthusiasm arrives late with one name still attached.

The trine lets both pull the same way, so the assumption nobody checks is the size of the thing, and with fire on both sides speed keeps being read as evidence the scope was right.

Explaining it more carefully does not reduce what is being handed over. The wording keeps improving while the objection stays exactly where it started.

Venus in Scorpio treats access to what somebody keeps hidden as the thing being negotiated, while Pluto in Aquarius moves control across a system rather than between two people. A square does not let either requirement stand down, so with both sides dug in the arrangement itself is what has to give.

Raised now, the terms get adjusted and the support continues; left alone, the support continues and the terms quietly stop matching it.

Venus in Libra measures an agreement by whether both sides are getting something comparable, and Jupiter in Leo gives generously enough to make one contribution stand out. A sextile makes the pair workable without obliging anyone to act, and because an immediate push is meeting a position that will not be given up, the terms carry the strain rather than the generosity.

The public version keeps getting larger while the private version keeps getting more precisely worded, and each attempt to reconcile them puts the gap back on display. Enthusiasm cannot close a gap that discretion is holding open. The distinction that helps is between what has been promised and what has been confirmed, because only one of those is being protected.

Mercury in Scorpio holds back until the phrasing is exact, because what gets said cannot be unsaid, while Jupiter in Leo commits to more than the work supports once the response is encouraging. The square refuses to let either requirement be quietly set aside, so the gap reappears in every attempt to close it, and pushing something guarded into public view raises the volume and not the safety.

Mercury in Scorpio chooses its words slowly because the result cannot be undone, and Mars in Leo pushes harder once recognition is part of what is at stake. The square leaves neither requirement anywhere to go, so every reply restates the same problem in a sharper tone while the decision itself does not move.

Shown that way the wider rule gets written; argued in the abstract it stays a preference nobody has to act on.

Mercury in Aquarius shows where a new rule would hold up across the group, and Venus in Sagittarius chooses the agreement that does not close off an independent plan. The sextile makes the pair workable without making it automatic, and since one requirement will not bend while the surrounding conditions keep shifting, a demonstration carries what an argument could not.

Tact and pressure are working together rather than against each other, which is why it moves at all. The ease is worth watching, because everyone can agree on the wording and still be describing different arrangements. What separates them is the phrase everybody accepts and the arrangement each side thinks it refers to.
